name: Siege of Fort St David / Pocock's Coromandel campaign
evidence: Pocock's squadron off Coromandel after the Battle of Cuddalore (29 Apr 1758). Daily positions 11.0-12.6N 80.4-82.6E, landmarks 'SADERASS' and 'FORT ST DAVIDS'. EncRem 'ALL THE FLEET IN COMPANY', 'ADMIRAL BORE DOWN TO THE...'. Fort St David fell on 2 Jun 1758. Newcastle (Capt. John Lloyd) sailed out with Steevens's reinforcement in 1757 (EncRem: Elizabeth, Yarmouth, Weymouth).

name: Capture of the Warwick by HMS Minerva
evidence: WarsAndFightsMemo, 23 Jan: 'BATTLE WITH FRENCH SHIP' at 45.33N 7.83W. EncRem, 24 Jan: 'WHAT WAS FORMALY THE WARWICK', then 'PRIZE IN COMPANY'. Capt. Alexander Hood.

name: Berbice slave uprising suppressed (Dutch naval expedition)
evidence: Anchored at 'POST ST ANDRIES' / Rio Berbice with the frigate St Maartensdijk (Capt. Maarten Haringman). Memo, 5 Dec 1763: 'REBELLEN!'. OtherRem: 'ZE GAAN EEN AANTAL PLANTAGES AF OM DE NEGEROPSTAND TE ONDERDRUKKEN'. CargoMemo, 1 Feb 1764: 72 'NEGERSLAVEN' shipped. 29 Jan 1764: 'EINDE EXPEDITIE'.

name: Byron takes possession of the Falklands (Port Egmont)
evidence: Dolphin (Cdre John Byron) at 51.45S 61.35W on 12 Jan 1765, then at anchor (no positions 13-26 Jan); landmark 'PORT EGMONT' from 27 Jan. Byron claimed the islands at Port Egmont on 23 Jan 1765.

name: Cook's first voyage arrives at Tahiti (Transit of Venus expedition)
evidence: Positions approaching Tahiti 10-12 Apr 1769 (17.6S 148.97W). On 13 Apr anchored at 'ROYAL BAY, GEORGES ISLAND' (Matavai Bay).

name: Dutch guard-ship policing the Gold/Slave Coast trade
evidence: Memo, 5 Jul 1771 at OUIDAH: 'CONTROLEREN PORTUGESE SCHEPEN OF ZE WEL TOL BETAALD HEBBEN TE ELMINA'. EncRem, 8 May 1771: a French snow from Gabon 'HAD 110 SLAVEN AAN BOORD'.

name: Cook's second voyage: first crossing of the Antarctic Circle
evidence: Position 66.60S 39.58E on 17 Jan 1773. OtherRem, 18 Jan: 'NOTHING TO THE S BUT ICE'. Easter Island landmark on 11 Mar 1774.

name: Phipps's Arctic expedition to Svalbard
evidence: Capt. Constantine John Phipps. Reached 80.8N in Jul 1773; anchored in 'VOGLE SOUND' 14-18 Jul; landmarks Hakluyt's Headland and Cloven Cliff.

name: Cevallos expedition: Spanish capture of Santa Catarina Island
evidence: Fourteen Spanish logbooks put ships 15-97 km from the island on 15-23 Feb 1777, anchored at 'SANTA CATALINA'. Poderoso, 18-19 Feb: 'COMBATE CON LA ESCUADRA ENEMIGA'. Marte, 21 Feb: 'NARRA LA RENDICIÓN DE LA ISLA DE SANTA CATHALINA'. Desconocido-15, 26 Feb: 'ENTREGA DE LA PLAZA POR PARTE DE LOS ENEMIGOS (PORTUGUESES)'. The expedition left Cádiz on 13 Nov 1776 under Casa Tilly in Poderoso; memos in Santa Teresa (MS. 1621) and Perpetua (MS. 2024) give '96 EMBARCACIONES MARCHANTES Y 20 DE GUERRA'.

name: First Battle of Ushant
evidence: Fireship Pluto (James Bradby) with Keppel's fleet. 24 Jul: 'OUR FLEET AND 40 SAILS OF FRENCH FLEET'; 25-29 Jul: 'BOTH FLEETS'. 27 Jul at 48.50N 8.38W, landmark Ushant.

name: Great Siege of Gibraltar: Spanish naval blockade
evidence: OtherRem, 8 Oct 1779 at 35.63N 8.20W: 'SALIDA DE CÁDIZ PARA EL BLOQUEO DE LA PLAZA DE GIBRALTAR... AL MANDO DEL EXCMO. SR. D. ANTONIO ULLOA'.

name: Moonlight Battle (Cape St Vincent)
evidence: Resolution 74 (Sir Chaloner Ogle) in Rodney's fleet, 'FLEET IN COMPANY' daily. 15 Jan at 37.58N 10.95W; landmark 'ST VINCENT' on 16 Jan and 'CAPE SPARTEL' on 18 Jan.

name: Battle of the Chesapeake (aftermath)
evidence: Montagu 74 (George Bowen) in Graves's fleet, landmark 'CAPE HENRY'. EncRem, 12 Sep 1781 at 36.62N 74.47W: 'TERRIBLE (BLOWN UP)'. HMS Terrible was scuttled after the battle on 11 Sep.

name: Battle of Cape Spartel
evidence: 11 Oct: 'SE PREPARAN PARA COMBATE NAVAL'. 20 Oct 1782 at 35.48N 6.88W: 'DESCRIBE CON DETALLE LA SITUACIÓN CON RELACIÓN A LA ESCUADRA ENEMIGA INGLESA Y LAS MANIOBRAS DE COMBATE'.

name: Relief of Malacca and conquest of Selangor (Van Braam's squadron)
evidence: Juno on the Malacca roads, 29 May 1784. Wassenaar off 'PONGER' (2.1N 102.3E), 5 Jun: 'DE AANVAL WAS HEVIG, DUURDE 3,5 UUR, VUURDEN 705 SCHOTEN'. 18 Jun: 'MET 23 LANDINGSVAARTUIGEN EN 700 MANSCHAPPEN... DE HELE SLAG OM MALAKKA WORDT VERTELD'. 2 Aug at Selangor: 'VEROVEREN SELANGOR'.

name: La Pérouse reaches Botany Bay as the First Fleet founds Sydney
evidence: Positions 33.72S 151.97E (23 Jan) and 34.19S 151.80E (24 Jan 1788). Voyage 'AVATSCHA -> NOUVELLE HOLLANDE'; memo on the 'LONGITUDE VRAIE D'ARRIVÉE À LA NOUVELLE HOLLANDE'. The French arrived on 24-26 Jan, while Phillip was moving the fleet to Port Jackson.

name: Nootka Crisis: Martínez occupies Nootka Sound
evidence: Arrived 3-4 May 1789 (49.67N 127.00W). OtherRem: 'EL DÍA 24 DE JUNIO SE TOMÓ POSESIÓN DEL PUERTO DE SAN LORENZO, SU COSTA E ISLAS ADYACENTES EN NOMBRE DEL REY'. Left on 31 Oct.

name: Spanish refortify Nootka; Fidalgo's Alaska expedition
evidence: Salvador Fidalgo anchored at 'NUTKA' on 4 Apr 1790. 8-17 Apr: 'SE DEDICAN A PONER UNA BATERIA EN LA PUNTA QUE RESGUARDA LA BOCA DEL PUERTO'. Then to Alaska; in Aug 1790 the log notes the Russian chief 'NESTRAT DELAROF' (Delarov).

name: Nootka Convention talks (Bodega y Quadra and Vancouver)
evidence: Jacinto Caamaño anchored at 'NOKA' 7 Sep-3 Oct 1792, during Vancouver's stay (28 Aug-12 Oct 1792).

name: Dutch East Indiamen captured off St Helena
evidence: 13 Jun 1795 at 15.3S 6.2W: 'ZIEN ZWARE SCHEPEN EN MAKEN KLAAR VOOR BATAILLE'. 14 Jun: 'WORDEN OPGEBRACHT DOOR DE ENGELSEN' (the data switches the ship's nationality to BRITISH).

name: Capitulation of Saldanha Bay (Lucas's Batavian squadron)
evidence: All nine ships are at or within 50 km of Saldanha Bay on 1-8 Aug 1796, anchored at 'SALDANHA BAAI'. Dordrecht is Lucas's own ship. Havick, 2 Aug: 'MAAKTEN KLAAR VOOR GEVECHT'. Revolutie is still at 'SALDANHA BAAY' on 17 Aug, the day of the surrender.

name: Action off Madeira: HMS Aimable against Sirène and Bergère
evidence: Capt. Henry Raper, escorting a convoy from Cork to Barbados. EncRem, 18 Dec 1799 at 31.25N 17.55W: 'ENGAGEMENT WITH FRENCH FRIGATE AND CORVETTE'.

name: Spanish frigate Orbe captures British whalers at the Galápagos
evidence: No positions in the log; the place is given as 'ISLA DE ALBIMOR EN LAS GALAPAGOS' (Albemarle, now Isabela). 7 Apr 1800: 'EL COMBATE EMPIEZA... ABORDAJE DE LAS NAVES ENEMIGAS (CASTOR Y BRETAÑA)'. Castor surrenders while her commander, William Anderson, is ashore.

name: Battle of Trafalgar
evidence: 3rd rate Swiftsure, Capt. William (Gordon) Rutherford, 'FLEET IN COMPANY' off Cádiz through Oct 1805. Position 36.00N 6.62W on 20 Oct; an entry for 21 Oct; anchored at Cádiz from 26 Oct.

name: Action of 13 March 1806 (capture of Marengo and Belle Poule)
evidence: Capt. William Parker. WarsAndFightsMemo, 13 Mar 1806: 'A BATTLE', at 26.77N 29.03W.

name: British invasions of the Río de la Plata
evidence: Lancaster (William Fothergill) brings a convoy from the Cape: Oct 1806 off Cape Santa Maria (34.0S 52.6W), 'CONVOY IN COMPANY'; at Maldonado in Apr 1807. Raisonable (Josias Rowley), voyage 'MONTEVIDEO -> TABLE BAY', 88 km from Montevideo on 2 Aug 1807.

name: French/Dutch frigate Nimph seizes a Spanish slaving schooner
evidence: WarsAndFightsMemo: 'NAMEN SPAANS SCHIP, EEN SCHOENER, IN BESLAG MET 11 NEGERJONGENS EN ENIGE VERVERSING, DE KAPITEIN MOCHT ZIJN REIS VERVOLGEN'. Capt. J.P.D. Scheidius, sailing from France to the Dutch East Indies.

name: British invasion of Java
evidence: Capt. Philip Beaver, with 'PRESIDENT & PHOEBE IN COMPANY'. Reaches 'JAVA, E-END' (7.90S 115.75E) on 13 Aug 1811; no positions while operating off Java; leaves via Button Rock (Sunda Strait) on 27 Sep. The London Gazette has Nisus, President and Phoebe taking Cheribon.

name: Barbados slave revolt (Bussa's Rebellion): Dutch brig sent
evidence: Memo: the brig Irene goes 'VIA BRABADOS (OM DAAR EEN SLAVENOPSTAND NEER TE SLAAN)'. 30 May, at Barbados: 'BLIJKT DE SLAVENOPSTAND AL GELUWD TE ZIJN'.

name: British hand Makassar back to the Dutch
evidence: Anchored at 'MAKASSER' 4 Sep-28 Oct 1816. 7 Oct: 'ENGELSCHE VLAG NEER, NEDERLANDSCHE VLAG GEHESEN... HET GOUVERNEMENT DOOR DEN ENGELSCHE RESIDENT... AAN DEN NED. GOUV. DEN HEER KRUITHOF OVERGING'; 'KONINNG VAN GOAH... KWAMEN TROUW ZWEREN'.

name: Pattimura uprising suppressed (Saparua and Haruku)
evidence: 25 May 1817, at HAROEKOE: 'VERDEDIGING ERVAN TEGEN OPSTANDELINGEN'. 26 Oct, at 'FORT DUURSTEDE, SAPAROEA': 'SCHIETEN OP OPSTANDELINGEN'.

name: Dutch punitive expedition to the Gold Coast (Ahanta)
evidence: At ST GEORGE D'ELMINA on 8 Jun and 29 Jul, and at BOUTRY on 17 Jul 1838. LifeOnBoard, 22 Aug: 'OVERLEED DE HEER GENERAAL MAJOOR J. VERVEER, OPPERBEVELHEBBER DER EXPEDITIE TER KUSTE VAN GUINEA'.

name: MCC slave voyage: GRENADIER (Middle Passage)
evidence: Elmina to Berbice: 'MET EEN LADING VAN 289 SLAVEN'; deaths numbered 'NO. 3, 4...'. From the logbook of the Middelburgsche Commercie Compagnie; track runs from the Gulf of Guinea to the Guianas.

name: MCC slave voyage: PRINS WILLEM V (Middle Passage)
evidence: 'OVERSTEEK NAAR SURINAME MET 256 LEVENDE SLAVEN'; deaths logged day by day in LifeOnBoard. From the logbook of the Middelburgsche Commercie Compagnie; track runs from the Gulf of Guinea to the Guianas.

name: MCC slave voyage: PHILADELPHIA (Middle Passage)
evidence: Guinea to Suriname: '224 SLAVEN AAN BOORD'. From the logbook of the Middelburgsche Commercie Compagnie; track runs from the Gulf of Guinea to the Guianas.

name: MCC slave voyage: DRIE GESUSTERS (Middle Passage)
evidence: Guinea to Suriname: '234 SLAVEN'; 12 death entries. From the logbook of the Middelburgsche Commercie Compagnie; track runs from the Gulf of Guinea to the Guianas.

name: MCC slave voyage: VLIEGENDE FAAM (Middle Passage)
evidence: Klein Popo/Elmina to Suriname. Revolt on board, 21 Dec 1756: 'OPSTAND ONDER DE SLAVEN OP HET SCHIP, DE MEESTER KOK EN DE SMID WORDEN DOODGESLAGEN'. From the logbook of the Middelburgsche Commercie Compagnie; track runs from the Gulf of Guinea to the Guianas.

name: MCC slave voyage: VROUWE JOHANNA CORES (Middle Passage)
evidence: Gulf of Guinea to Suriname: deaths numbered up to 'NO. 66-70' (38 CargoMemo entries). From the logbook of the Middelburgsche Commercie Compagnie; track runs from the Gulf of Guinea to the Guianas.

name: MCC slave voyage: EENIGHEIJT (Middle Passage)
evidence: Elmina to Suriname: '319 SLAVEN'. From the logbook of the Middelburgsche Commercie Compagnie; track runs from the Gulf of Guinea to the Guianas.

name: MCC slave voyage: EENIGHEIJT (Middle Passage)
evidence: Ivory Coast to Suriname: '203 LEVENDIGE SLAVEN AAN BOORD. ZE HEBBER ER 256 GEKOCHT. ER ZIJN ER INMIDDELS 53 OVERLEDEN'. From the logbook of the Middelburgsche Commercie Compagnie; track runs from the Gulf of Guinea to the Guianas.

name: MCC slave voyage: VROUWE JOHANNA CORES (Middle Passage)
evidence: Elmina to Suriname. 18 Jan 1765: 'EEN OPSTAND DOOR DE SLAVEN WERD DOOR ENKELE SLAVINNEN BEKEND GEMAAKT'. From the logbook of the Middelburgsche Commercie Compagnie; track runs from the Gulf of Guinea to the Guianas.

name: MCC slave voyage: VLIEGENDE FAAM (Middle Passage)
evidence: Guinea to Suriname: 'NU 203 SLAVEN IN HET SCHIP'. From the logbook of the Middelburgsche Commercie Compagnie; track runs from the Gulf of Guinea to the Guianas.

name: MCC slave voyage: HAAST U LANGZAAM (Middle Passage)
evidence: West Africa to Suriname: 'LADING VAN 262 SLAVEN (MINUS 7 OVERLEDEN)'. From the logbook of the Middelburgsche Commercie Compagnie; track runs from the Gulf of Guinea to the Guianas.

name: MCC slave voyage: HAAST U LANGZAAM (Middle Passage)
evidence: West Africa to Suriname: 'LADING VAN 281 (MINUS 6) SLAVEN'. From the logbook of the Middelburgsche Commercie Compagnie; track runs from the Gulf of Guinea to the Guianas.

name: MCC slave voyage: GEERTUIJDA EN CHRISTINA (Middle Passage)
evidence: 'VERTREKKEN MET 276 SLAVEN VAN ELMINA NAAR SURINAME. ER ZIJN VOOR DE AFRIKAANSE KUST 34 SLAVEN OVERLEDEN'; deaths numbered to 128. From the logbook of the Middelburgsche Commercie Compagnie; track runs from the Gulf of Guinea to the Guianas.

name: MCC slave voyage: VERGENOEGEN (Middle Passage)
evidence: Elmina to Suriname: '242 SLAVEN', counted down day by day. From the logbook of the Middelburgsche Commercie Compagnie; track runs from the Gulf of Guinea to the Guianas.

name: MCC slave voyage: STANDVASTIGHEID (Middle Passage)
evidence: Elmina to Suriname: '101 MANNEN, 78 VROUWEN, 27 JONGENS EN 20 MEISJES' (226). From the logbook of the Middelburgsche Commercie Compagnie; track runs from the Gulf of Guinea to the Guianas.

name: MCC slave voyage: VERGENOEGEN (Middle Passage)
evidence: Loango to Suriname: '393 SLAVEN INGEKOCHT, 26 DAARVAN AAN POKKEN EN BLOEDLOOP VERLOREN'. From the logbook of the Middelburgsche Commercie Compagnie; track runs from the Gulf of Guinea to the Guianas.
